fullPassage:
Letters from Recent Graduates

Welcome to a new season of High School Magazine. To start off the new school year on the right foot, we asked some of our recent graduates to give us tips on how to succeed in the coming year and beyond.

Compare Apples to Apples
Nahyeon Kim Class of 2024

In high school, everyone told me how talented an artist I was, so I dreamed of becoming an illustrator. In university, though, everyone seemed much more talented than me, and they all worked so hard that I felt small in comparison. I thought about giving up my dream of becoming an artist. Then one day, I happened to see a drawing I had won an award for from middle school on the kitchen wall. I was embarrassed because it wasn't very good.

People say you shouldn't compare apples to oranges, and they're right. That's why it doesn't make sense to compare yourself to Internet personalities or even people in your real life. Maybe they had an advantage, or even a disadvantage, that you didn't. If you are going to compare yourself to anyone, the only fair comparison is "yesterday-you." Only you know where you started and how much effort you've put in. I couldn't see the progress in my ability when I only compared myself to others. Everyone develops differently. I'm able to see now the drawing in the kitchen was full of mistakes that I no longer make. It is empowering to see how I have improved rather than to envy the success of others. Your competition isn't the person next door or the influencer on social media: it's you.

Don't Be Afraid to Speak Up
Elias Walter Class of 2025

Do you share your opinion in class discussions, or do you just stay silent and keep it to yourself? Like many of you, I often found myself in the second group. A little black hole inside of me swallowed my voice when I considered speaking up. The consequences of being ridiculed or being wrong were always on my mind.

Then, after a particularly heated conversation in class, I asked myself, "What am I afraid of?" I was scared that bad things would happen, but I never thought about good things. When I noticed others taking risks, I knew that I needed to do the same in order to participate. Many people are scared to speak up, but a lot of them do it anyway because they think it's worth it. So I left my comfort zone and started to speak up. I grew intellectually and socially by expressing myself more clearly. I got closer to friends who liked how open I was with them. Now I have more people with whom I can talk, share my ideas, and learn new things. Remember, taking the risk of expressing yourself can be extremely rewarding in unexpected ways.

Use Energy on What You Can Control
Abigail Princeton Class of 2022

As I worked through my second year into my third in college, I had more troubles balancing school and personal life. I would get excited, anxious, worried, and bored all at once and then separately. I would get exhausted when I had to write a report for my courses, mediate a disaster between friends, and respond to the comments on my online journal. I was drowning in a sea of responsibilities, concerns, and anxieties, and that was when I read an article with a simple insight.

The article advised me to draw two big circles, with myself in the center. The smaller circle is my circle of influence, and I have direct control over the things inside it: what I eat and drink, how I behave, or what I do after school. The bigger circle is called my circle of concern: things I worry about but have no direct control over. For example, I have no direct control over how my professor will react to my report, but I do have control over the amount of research I do for it. Believing that everything was in my circle of influence left me stressed out and constantly exhausted. By wasting less energy on my circle of concern, I was able to invest more energy into things that mattered. I no longer worry about what my friends think, and I focus on my own actions. I don't get anxious over what might be on the test, and instead I put in every effort to understand the concepts themselves. Now, I only put my mental and physical energy into my circle of influence: eating healthy, staying in shape, and working hard.

questions.passage: In high school, everyone told me how talented an artist I was, so I dreamed of becoming an (A)[illustrator / instructor]. In university, though, everyone seemed much more talented than me, and they all worked so hard that I felt small in (B)[comparison / competition]. I thought about giving up my dream of becoming an artist. Then one day, I happened to see a drawing I had won an award for from middle school on the kitchen wall. I was (C)[embarrassed / encouraged] because it wasn't very good.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 나는 삽화가(illustrator)가 되는 꿈을 꿨고, 비교(comparison)해서 작게 느꼈으며, 그림이 좋지 않아서 부끄러웠다(embarrassed).
det.analysis:
✅ ① illustrator — comparison — embarrassed: 원문 그대로
❌ ② instructor(강사): illustrator(삽화가)와 철자 유사하지만 의미 다름, encouraged(격려된): 그림이 좋지 않았으므로 부적절
❌ ③ competition(경쟁): comparison(비교)이 원문
❌ ④ instructor+competition+encouraged: 모두 원문과 다름
det.tip: illustrator(삽화가) vs instructor(강사) — 철자 유사 혼동 주의! in comparison = 비교해서

questions.passage: I'm able to see now the drawing in the kitchen was full of mistakes that I no longer make. It is (A)[empowering / weakening] to see how I have improved rather than to envy the success of others. Your (B)[competition / cooperation] isn't the person next door or the (C)[influencer / instructor] on social media: it's you.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 내가 얼마나 발전했는지 보는 것은 힘을 주는(empowering) 일이다. 당신의 경쟁 상대(competition)는 옆집 사람이나 소셜 미디어의 인플루언서(influencer)가 아니라 바로 당신이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ empowering — competition — influencer: 원문 일치
❌ ① weakening(약하게 하는): empowering(힘을 주는)의 반의어
❌ ② cooperation(협력): competition(경쟁)의 반의어
❌ ④ 세 단어 모두 원문과 반대
det.tip: empowering(힘을 주는) ↔ weakening(약화시키는), competition(경쟁) ↔ cooperation(협력)

questions.passage: A little black hole inside of me swallowed my voice when I considered speaking up. The (A)[consequences / benefits] of being ridiculed or being wrong were always on my mind. Then, after a particularly heated conversation in class, I asked myself, 'What am I afraid of?' Many people are scared to speak up, but a lot of them do it anyway because they think it's (B)[worth / worthless] it. So I left my (C)[comfort zone / danger zone] and started to speak up.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 조롱당하거나 틀리는 것의 결과(consequences)가 항상 마음에 있었다. 그들은 그것이 가치 있다고(worth) 생각하기 때문이다. 나는 안전지대(comfort zone)를 떠나 말하기 시작했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② consequences — worth — comfort zone: 원문 일치
❌ ① benefits(이점): 조롱/오류의 결과이므로 부정적 맥락에 부적합
❌ ③ worthless(가치 없는): worth(가치 있는)의 반의어
❌ ④ benefits+worthless+danger zone: 모두 원문과 다름
det.tip: consequences = 결과(부정적 뉘앙스). comfort zone = 안전지대. leave one's comfort zone = 안전지대를 벗어나다

questions.passage: As I worked through my second year into my third in college, I had more troubles ①<u>balancing</u> school and personal life. I would get excited, anxious, worried, and bored all at once and then separately. I would get ②<u>energized</u> when I had to write a report for my courses, ③<u>mediate</u> a disaster between friends, and respond to the comments on my online journal. I was drowning in a sea of ④<u>responsibilities</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 보고서를 쓰고, 친구 사이를 중재하고, 댓글에 답해야 할 때 지쳐갔다(exhausted). energized(활기 넘치는)는 exhausted(지친)의 반의어이므로 부적절하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② energized(활기 넘치는) → exhausted(지친)이 원문. 과중한 업무로 지치는 문맥에 energized는 부적절
❌ ① balancing(균형 잡기): 원문 그대로
❌ ③ mediate(중재하다): 원문 그대로
❌ ④ responsibilities(책임): 원문 그대로
det.tip: exhausted(지친) ↔ energized(활기 넘치는). drowning in responsibilities = 책임에 허덕이는 → 지치는 문맥

questions.passage: People say you shouldn't compare apples to oranges, and they're right. That's why it doesn't make sense to compare yourself to Internet personalities or even people in your real life. Maybe they had an ①<u>advantage</u>, or even a disadvantage, that you didn't. If you are going to compare yourself to anyone, the only fair ②<u>comparison</u> is 'yesterday-you.' I couldn't see the ③<u>decline</u> in my ability when I only compared myself to others. Everyone ④<u>develops</u> differently.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 나 자신을 다른 사람과만 비교할 때 내 능력의 발전(progress)을 볼 수 없었다. decline(쇠퇴)은 progress(발전)의 반의어이므로 부적절하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ decline(쇠퇴) → progress(발전)이 원문. 자신의 성장을 볼 수 없었다는 문맥
❌ ① advantage(이점): 원문 그대로
❌ ② comparison(비교): 원문 그대로
❌ ④ develops(발전하다): 원문 그대로
det.tip: progress(발전, 진전) ↔ decline(쇠퇴, 감소). see the progress = 발전을 보다

questions.passage: The article advised me to draw two big circles, with myself in the center. The smaller circle is my circle of ①<u>influence</u>, and I have direct control over the things inside it. The bigger circle is called my circle of ②<u>concern</u>: things I worry about but have no direct control over. Believing that everything was in my circle of influence left me ③<u>relaxed</u> and constantly exhausted. By wasting less energy on my circle of concern, I was able to ④<u>invest</u> more energy into things that mattered.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 모든 것이 내 영향력의 원 안에 있다고 믿는 것은 나를 스트레스 받게(stressed out) 만들었다. relaxed(편안한)는 stressed out(스트레스 받는)의 반의어이므로 부적절하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ relaxed(편안한) → stressed out(스트레스 받는)이 원문. 모든 것을 통제하려니 스트레스를 받는 문맥
❌ ① influence(영향력): 원문 그대로
❌ ② concern(걱정): 원문 그대로
❌ ④ invest(투자하다): 원문 그대로
det.tip: stressed out(스트레스 받는) ↔ relaxed(편안한). left me stressed out = 나를 스트레스 받게 만들었다

questions.passage: A little black hole inside of me swallowed my voice when I considered speaking up. The consequences of being __________ or being wrong were always on my mind. Then, after a particularly heated conversation in class, I asked myself, 'What am I afraid of?'
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 조롱당하거나(ridiculed) 틀리는 것의 결과가 항상 마음에 있었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ ridiculed(조롱당하는): being wrong과 병렬로 부정적 결과. 말하기를 두려워하는 문맥에 적합
❌ ① praised(칭찬받는): 두려움의 원인이 아님
❌ ② supported(지지받는): 두려움의 원인이 아님
❌ ③ rewarded(보상받는): 두려움의 원인이 아님
det.tip: ridiculed = 조롱당한. ridicule = 비웃다, 조롱하다. being ridiculed or being wrong = 부정적 결과 두 가지

questions.passage: I grew intellectually and socially by expressing myself more clearly. I got closer to friends who liked how open I was with them. Now I have more people with whom I can talk, share my ideas, and learn new things. Remember, taking the risk of expressing yourself can be extremely __________ in unexpected ways.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 자신을 표현하는 위험을 감수하는 것은 예상치 못한 방식으로 극도로 보람 있을(rewarding) 수 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ rewarding(보람 있는): 지적/사회적 성장, 친구와 가까워짐 등 긍정적 결과에 적합
❌ ① damaging(해로운): 긍정적 결과를 서술하는 문맥에 부적합
❌ ② exhausting(지치게 하는): 보람 있다는 긍정적 결론에 부적합
❌ ④ embarrassing(당혹스러운): 긍정적 결론에 부적합
det.tip: rewarding = 보람 있는, 보상이 있는. reward(보상) + -ing. 위험을 감수한 결과 → 긍정적 보상

questions.passage: I would get exhausted when I had to write a report for my courses, mediate a disaster between friends, and respond to the comments on my online journal. I was drowning in a sea of responsibilities, concerns, and anxieties, and that was when I read an article with a simple __________. The article advised me to draw two big circles, with myself in the center. The smaller circle is my circle of influence, and I have direct control over the things inside it. The bigger circle is called my circle of concern.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 그때 나는 간단한 통찰(insight)이 담긴 기사를 읽었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② insight(통찰): 원문 그대로. 두 원 그리기라는 깨달음/통찰에 적합
❌ ① complaint(불평): 기사가 조언을 주는 문맥에 부적합
❌ ③ obstacle(장애물): 해결책을 제시하는 문맥에 부적합
❌ ④ illusion(환상): simple insight와 어울리지 않음
det.tip: insight = 통찰, 깨달음. a simple insight = 간단한 깨달음. in + sight = 안을 들여다봄

questions.passage: In university, though, everyone seemed much more talented than me, and they all worked so hard that I felt small in comparison. I thought about giving up my dream of becoming an artist. Then one day, I happened to see a drawing I had won an award for from middle school on the kitchen wall. I was <u>embarrassed</u> because it wasn't very good.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 embarrassed와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 그림이 별로 좋지 않았기 때문에 부끄러웠다(embarrassed).
det.analysis:
✅ ① ashamed(부끄러운): embarrassed의 동의어
❌ ② delighted(기쁜): embarrassed의 반의어
❌ ③ relieved(안도한): embarrassed와 무관
❌ ④ confident(자신감 있는): embarrassed의 반의어
det.tip: embarrassed = ashamed = 부끄러운, 창피한

questions.passage: I was drowning in a sea of responsibilities, concerns, and <u>anxieties</u>, and that was when I read an article with a simple insight.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 anxieties와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 나는 책임, 걱정, 그리고 불안(anxieties)의 바다에 빠져 있었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ worries(걱정거리): anxieties의 동의어
❌ ① comforts(위안): anxieties의 반의어
❌ ② pleasures(즐거움): anxieties의 반의어
❌ ③ certainties(확신): anxieties의 반의어
det.tip: anxieties = worries = concerns = 걱정, 불안. anxiety(불안) → anxieties(복수형)

questions.passage: By wasting less energy on my circle of concern, I was able to <u>invest</u> more energy into things that mattered.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 invest와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 나는 중요한 일에 더 많은 에너지를 투자할(invest) 수 있었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② devote(바치다/헌신하다): invest와 동의어. 에너지를 투입한다는 의미
❌ ① waste(낭비하다): invest의 반의어
❌ ③ withdraw(철수하다): invest와 반대 방향
❌ ④ ignore(무시하다): 에너지 투입과 무관
det.tip: invest = devote = put into = 투자하다, 쏟다. invest energy into = 에너지를 ~에 쏟다

questions.passage: Maybe they had an <u>advantage</u>, or even a disadvantage, that you didn't. If you are going to compare yourself to anyone, the only fair comparison is 'yesterday-you.'
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 advantage와 의미가 반대인 것은?

det.korean: 그들에게는 당신에게 없는 이점(advantage)이 있었을 수도 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ drawback(단점): advantage의 반의어
❌ ① benefit(이점): advantage의 동의어
❌ ② strength(강점): advantage의 동의어
❌ ③ merit(장점): advantage의 동의어
det.tip: advantage(이점) ↔ drawback/disadvantage(단점). 원문에서도 advantage와 disadvantage를 대조

questions.passage: It is <u>empowering</u> to see how I have improved rather than to envy the success of others.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 empowering과 의미가 반대인 것은?

det.korean: 내가 얼마나 발전했는지 보는 것은 힘을 주는(empowering) 일이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ discouraging(의기소침하게 하는): empowering의 반의어
❌ ① inspiring(영감을 주는): empowering의 동의어
❌ ② motivating(동기를 부여하는): empowering의 동의어
❌ ④ uplifting(기분을 고양시키는): empowering의 동의어
det.tip: empowering(힘을 주는) ↔ discouraging(의기소침하게 하는). empower = 힘을 주다, 권한을 부여하다

questions.passage:
(A) I thought about <u>giving up</u> my dream of becoming an artist. Then one day, I happened to see a drawing I had won an award for from middle school on the kitchen wall. I was embarrassed because it wasn't very good. People say you shouldn't compare apples to oranges, and they're right.

(B) The volunteers spent the entire afternoon <u>giving out</u> supplies to families affected by the flood. They organized boxes of food, water, and blankets, making sure everyone received what they needed.
questions.stem: 다음 (A)와 (B)에서 밑줄 친 giving up / giving out의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) 예술가가 되려는 꿈을 포기하는 것(giving up)을 생각했다. (B) 자선 행사는 노인들에게 무료 식사를 나누어 주는(giving out) 것에 초점을 맞추었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 포기하다 — 나누어 주다: (A) give up = 포기하다, (B) give out = 나누어 주다/배포하다
❌ ① 주다 — 포기하다: (A)와 (B)의 의미가 뒤바뀜
❌ ③ 포기하다 — 포기하다: (B)는 give out(배포하다)
❌ ④ 나누어 주다 — 포기하다: (A)와 (B)의 의미가 뒤바뀜
det.tip: give up = 포기하다, give out = 나누어 주다/배포하다. give의 구동사에 따라 의미가 달라진다

questions.stem:
다음 영영 풀이에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"a person who draws illustrations, especially for books or magazines"

det.korean: 특히 책이나 잡지를 위해 삽화를 그리는 사람 = 삽화가(illustrator)
det.analysis:
✅ ① illustrator(삽화가): 정의에 정확히 부합
❌ ② instructor(강사): 가르치는 사람
❌ ③ influencer(인플루언서): 영향력 있는 사람
❌ ④ interpreter(통역사): 통역하는 사람
det.tip: illustrator = 삽화가. illustrate(삽화를 그리다) + -or(~하는 사람). illustration = 삽화

questions.passage: In high school, everyone told me how talented an artist I was, so I dreamed of becoming an illustrator. In university, though, everyone seemed much more talented than me, and they all worked so hard that I felt small in __________ (compare).
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: 나는 비교(comparison)해서 작게 느꼈다.
det.analysis: compare(동사: 비교하다) → comparison(명사: 비교). 전치사 in 뒤에 명사가 필요하므로 명사형으로 변환.
det.tip: compare(v.) → comparison(n.). in comparison = 비교해서. -ison 접미사로 명사화

questions.passage: Many people are scared to speak up, but a lot of them do it anyway because they think it's worth it. So I left my comfort zone and started to speak up. I grew __________ (intellect) and socially by expressing myself more clearly. I got closer to friends who liked how open I was with them. Now I have more people with whom I can talk, share my ideas, and learn new things.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: 나는 자신을 더 명확하게 표현함으로써 지적으로(intellectually) 그리고 사회적으로 성장했다.
det.analysis: intellect(명사: 지성) → intellectually(부사: 지적으로). grew를 수식하는 부사 필요. socially와 병렬.
det.tip: intellect(n. 지성) → intellectual(adj. 지적인) → intellectually(adv. 지적으로). 동사 grew를 수식 → 부사형

questions.passage: People say you shouldn't compare apples to oranges, and they're right. That's why it doesn't make sense to compare yourself to Internet personalities or even people in your real life. If you are going to compare yourself to anyone, the only fair comparison is __________. Only you know where you started and how much effort you've put in.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 자신을 누군가와 비교하려면, 유일하게 공정한 비교 대상은 '어제의 나(yesterday-you)'이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ "yesterday-you": 원문 그대로. 자신의 과거와 비교하라는 메시지
❌ ① your best friend(가장 친한 친구): 타인과 비교하지 말라는 문맥에 부적합
❌ ② a famous celebrity(유명 연예인): Internet personalities처럼 비교 대상에서 제외
❌ ③ your classmate(반 친구): 타인 비교에 해당
det.tip: the only fair comparison is 'yesterday-you' = 유일하게 공정한 비교는 어제의 나. 자기 성장에 초점

questions.passage: As I worked through my second year into my third in college, I had more troubles balancing school and personal life. I was drowning in a sea of responsibilities, concerns, and anxieties. The article advised me to draw two big circles. The smaller circle is my circle of influence. The bigger circle is called my circle of concern: things I worry about but have __________. Believing that everything was in my circle of influence left me stressed out and constantly exhausted.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 더 큰 원은 관심의 원으로, 걱정은 하지만 직접적인 통제권이 없는(no direct control over) 것들이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① no direct control over: 원문 그대로. 관심의 원 = 통제 불가능한 걱정 영역
❌ ② complete authority over(완전한 권한): 이는 영향력의 원에 해당
❌ ③ great influence on(큰 영향력): 관심의 원은 통제 불가능한 영역
❌ ④ strong opinions about(강한 의견): 통제와 관련 없음
det.tip: circle of concern = 관심의 원 (통제 불가). circle of influence = 영향력의 원 (통제 가능). 핵심 대비
